title.narrative: Asia Counter Trafficking In Persons (USAID Asia CTIP)

description.narrative: (USAID Regional Development Mission-Asia (RDM/A)): The USAID Asia Countering Trafficking In Persons (Asia CTIP) activity is part of a comprehensive U.S. government effort to address transnational and regional challenges to combat trafficking in persons. The activity has an overarching goal of facilitating an Asia region that more effectively addresses human trafficking risks and responses that transcend national borders through three priorities: 1) enhanced awareness and understanding regarding trafficking in persons and effective responses, 2) improved coordination and cooperation between source, transit and destination countries, and 3) engagement with the private sector to reduce trafficking in persons in targeted sectors. USAID Asia CTIP promotes free and open commerce within a rules-based environment that protects and promotes labor rights and advances the interests of U.S. companies. The activity also addresses exploitative practices that fund transnational criminal networks and destabilize the region..With FY 2022 funding, USAID Asia CTIP will focus on: 1) conducting needs assessments, studies, evaluations, and other information-gathering efforts to improve reporting and harmonization of CTIP monitoring and evaluation indicators across Asia, as well as building the capacity of academics, local research organizations, think tanks, and investigative journalists to produce high-quality regional analysis on trafficking in persons across the region; 2) increasing information sharing and harmonization of national trafficking definitions, laws, and penalties among the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) member states, and assisting member states in complying with their commitments under regional conventions and frameworks; and 3) collaborating with the private sector to reduce opportunities for trafficking in persons and forced labor in target sectors..
